items.title: 14.5.1 Impact of burning fossil fuels on the atmosphere

blocks.text: The burning of fossil fuels is the primary cause of current climate change, altering the earth's ecosystems and causing human and environmental health problems. It affects the earth system in several ways, including greenhouse gas emissions, air pollution and volatile organic compounds (Figure 14.2).

blocks.alt: A simple landscape. A power station chimney gives off SO2, a car NO2 and a livestock farm NH3 (red arrows rising). The gases change into particles and aerosols of SO4 2-, NO3- and NH4+. Some settle straight onto the ground and a lake (dry deposition, blue arrow); others are washed down by rain from a cloud onto a forest (wet deposition, acid rain).
blocks.caption: Impacts of air pollutants on the atmosphere (original diagram after Figure 14.2).
